3
The power output P of a star can be modelled with the equation
P = AT 4
where  is a constant, A is the surface area of the star and T is the surface temperature of the
star.
What are the SI base units of ?
A
kg s–2
K–4
K–4
B
kg s–3
C
kg m–1
s–2
K–4
s–3
D
kg m–1
K–4

hints: Start from $P = \sigma AT^4$ and rearrange to $\sigma = P/(AT^4)$, so you need the base units of power $P$, area $A$ and temperature $T$.
Recall power in SI base units is $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$, area is $\text{m}^2$, and $T^4$ contributes $\text{K}^4$ in the denominator.
Divide the power units by $\text{m}^2\text{ K}^4$ and cancel $\text{m}^2$ to leave only $\text{kg}$, $\text{s}$ and $\text{K}$ powers.
walkthrough: Write the equation with $\sigma$ as the subject: $\sigma = P/(AT^4)$, so the units of $\sigma$ are the units of $P$ divided by the units of $AT^4$.

State the SI base units of each term: power $P$ has units of watt, which is $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$, surface area $A$ has units $\text{m}^2$, and temperature $T$ has base unit $\text{K}$ so $T^4$ has units $\text{K}^4$.
Substitute these units into the rearranged equation: units of $\sigma = (\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3})/(\text{m}^2\text{ K}^4)$.
Cancel $\text{m}^2$ top and bottom, leaving $\text{kg s}^{-3}\text{ K}^{-4}$ with no metre term remaining.
Check homogeneity: $\text{kg s}^{-3}\text{K}^{-4}$ multiplied by $\text{m}^2\text{ K}^4$ returns $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$, which is power. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives $\text{s}^{-2}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$, which would correspond to energy divided by area and $T^4$ rather than power divided by area and $T^4$.

B.explanation: Matches $\sigma = P/(AT^4)$ with $P$ in $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $T^4$ in $\text{K}^4$, leaving $\text{kg s}^{-3}\text{K}^{-4}$.

C.explanation: Includes an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ and only $\text{s}^{-2}$, so the metre and second powers do not balance $P = \sigma AT^4$.

D.explanation: Includes an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ because the $\text{m}^2$ from power and the $\text{m}^2$ from area have not been fully cancelled.
